prerequisites: Master certain mathematical and physical knowledge
Have consolidated the concepts covered in the subjects Mechanics of Materials, Elasticity and Advanced Mechanics of Materials, and Design and Calculation of Structures

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basic tools to face the design and execution of the most common reinforced concrete structural elements.
Understand the mechanical behavior of the materials that constitute reinforced concrete.
Understand the resistant behavior and the various calculation models of concrete structures, analyzing the most common reinforced concrete elements.
Develop strategies for solving various reinforced concrete elements.
Facilitate the handling of applicable regulations.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION. Structural Code CE-21. Scope of application of the instruction. Previous considerations. Certification. Units and measures. Project documents. General principles.

REINFORCED CONCRETE MATERIALS. Cements, water, aggregates, admixtures and additions. Fundamental parameters of concrete: compressive strength, maximum aggregate size, consistency, exposure environment. Stress/strain diagrams of concrete. Passive reinforcement: mechanical characteristics, bond characteristics, ductility, weldability. Deformed bars, welded wire mesh and basic welded lattice reinforcement.

BASES OF CALCULATION. Performance requirements. Calculation of forces. Limit state method: ultimate limit state and service limit states. Actions on the structure: classification and combination of loads. Design strength.
ULTIMATE LIMIT STATE UNDER NORMAL STRESSES. General considerations. Bases of calculation. Rectangular stress block diagram. Section deformation domains. Equilibrium equations. Interaction diagrams.

SIMPLIFIED METHOD FOR CALCULATING FLEXION SECTIONS. Equilibrium conditions. Limit depth of the neutral axis. Mechanical capacity of the reinforcement. Limit moment and design moment. Minimum reinforcement ratios.
PLACEMENT OF PASSIVE REINFORCEMENT. Bending of passive reinforcement. Distance between bars. Anchoring of reinforcement. Concrete cover. Spacers, relative arrangements of reinforcement.

ULTIMATE LIMIT STATE FOR SHEAR. General considerations. Obtaining the effective shear force. Strut-and-tie model. Checking oblique compression of the web. Checking tension in the web. Shift of the bending moment diagram. Reinforcement arrangement.
SERVICE LIMIT STATES. General considerations. Types of deflection. Cracking moment. Calculation of instantaneous and deferred deflection. Cracking limit state.
STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS. Beams, footings, columns, walls.
Classroom practices, with the development of problems related to each topic developed in the theoretical lectures.
Classes and/or seminars for solving practical exercises.
teaching_methods: Assessment activities (monitoring, problem-solving, case defense, written exam)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation, tutoring follow-up, and proactive attitude
Final exam (alternative path for 100% of grade)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of a practical work (25%), attendance and participation (10%), a practical exam (15%), and a written exam on general knowledge (50%). Alternatively, students can obtain 100% of their grade through a final exam, in which case they cannot opt for the participation grade. In the second call, grades for tutorials, practical work, exposure, and defense are maintained from the first call and are not recoverable. Students attending the second call must repeat the practical and written exam, or the final exam if they chose that option in the first call.
